look_here_first: Check multiple mature leaf lobe tips: usually rounded with NO terminal bristle. If the leaf lacks a clear cross-shaped outline, look at thick (2–5 mm), often yellowish, densely stellate-hairy twigs and the harsh/stippled LOWER leaf surface with crowded yellowish glandular hairs plus minute stellate hairs. Confirm small reddish-brown buds (usually ≤4 mm) and scaly light-gray bark.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Deciduous tree of dry uplands, ridges, prairies, clays, sands, and limestone hills.

key_traits.label: Twigs
key_traits.text: Typically thick/yellowish with stellate pubescence; useful when leaf outline is atypical.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Frequently cruciform/cross-shaped with broad squarish middle lobes, but shape is variable; lower surface densely harsh with stellate hairs.

key_traits.label: Acorn
key_traits.text: Cup deeply saucer-shaped and may enclose roughly one-quarter to two-thirds of the nut.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaf blade typically 40–150 × 20–100 mm, lobes rounded or spatulate, distal two lobes often nearly perpendicular to midrib (cross shape variable).

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaf underside includes crowded yellowish glandular hairs and scattered minute 6–8-rayed appressed/semiappressed stellate hairs; often harsh, NOT densely velvety.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Twigs usually 2–5 mm thick, densely stellate-pubescent, yellowish or grayish; terminal buds reddish brown, to 4 mm, sparsely pubescent.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Acorn cup deeply saucer-shaped, about 7–12(–18) mm deep × 10–15(–25) mm wide, tightly appressed scales, 1/4–2/3 of nut; nut 10–20 mm long.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: White-oak-group acorns typically mature in the first growing season (annual), unlike blackjack oak's biennial fruit.
